newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Oct industry orders up after Sept slump.
newsitem.headline: German Oct industry orders up after Sept slump.

text.p: German industrial orders rose 2.9 percent in October after a 3.4 percent fall in September, the Federal Statistics Office said on Wednesday, contrasting with output data released on Tuesday which showed a sharp drop.

The figures, seasonally adjusted and provisional, are often erratic and usually treated with scepticism by analysts. But they do offer an early glimpse of how the German economy is likely to perform in the current fourth quarter.
October industry orders were up 6.4 percent year-on-year, calculated against Bundesbank historical data, after a 1.1 percent fall in September.
Earlier, gross domestic product data for the third quarter showed a gain of one percent over the previous quarter and a rise of 2.4 percent against a year earlier.
Foreign orders -- the main engine of Germany's economic recovery -- rose by 3.8 percent in October against the previous month. Domestic orders also picked up by 2.3 percent.
Capital goods orders were most robust, up 4.3 percent, while intermediate and consumer goods orders grew more slowly.
Despite the pickup, orders in September and October were down two percent against the two preceding months, but still up by 3.7 percent against the same period in 1995.

West German industry orders were up 3.4 percent month-on-month in October, while the east German figure was down three percent against September and a sharp 10.3 percent below the same month a year earlier.
